exact_channel_interface: Every L-R edge is a port edge: E(L,R)=X subseteq P_L x P_R.
There are no vertices outside L union R union {z}.
No condition is imposed on internal edges of G[L] or G[R], or on other z-L / z-R adjacencies.
abstract_object.invariant: k := nu(X), the maximum matching number of X.

layer_1_exact_local_channel_theorem.name: EXACT_LOCAL_CHANNEL_THEOREM

lower_bound: Let M be a maximum matching in X of size k.
For every uv in M, c-u-v-f is a c-f path.
Because M is a matching, these k direct paths are pairwise internally vertex-disjoint.
The hub path c-z-f is internally vertex-disjoint from all direct paths because z is outside P_L union P_R.
upper_bound: Let U be a minimum vertex cover of bipartite X.
Delete {z} union U. The hub path is destroyed by deleting z.
Every L-R edge lies in X and every X-edge meets U, so no L-R edge survives.
Because c notin P_L and f notin P_R, neither anchor is deleted by U.
Thus c and f lie in different components of G-({z} union U).

dependencies: Konig theorem for finite bipartite graphs

layer_2A_block_quotient_transfer_theorem.name: TWO_BLOCK_CHANNEL_LOCAL_TO_GLOBAL_TRANSFER_THEOREM__BLOCK_QUOTIENT
layer_2A_block_quotient_transfer_theorem.purpose: Simple compositional sufficient theorem when each surviving block remains internally connected.

definitions.deletion_budget: k=nu(X). Consider every S subseteq V(G) with |S|<=k.
definitions.BLOCK_ROBUSTNESS: Whenever L-S is nonempty, G[L-S] is connected; whenever R-S is nonempty, G[R-S] is connected.
block_interface_graph_BS: Vertices are the surviving nonempty modules among L-S, R-S, and {z} if z notin S.
L-R is an edge iff at least one X-edge has both endpoints outside S.
z-L is an edge iff z notin S and z has a neighbor in L-S.
z-R is an edge iff z notin S and z has a neighbor in R-S.
definitions.INTERFACE_ROBUSTNESS: For every |S|<=k, B_S is connected on its surviving modules.

layer_2A_block_quotient_transfer_theorem.quotient_lemma: Under BLOCK_ROBUSTNESS, for every such S, G-S is connected iff B_S is connected.
theorem: If BLOCK_ROBUSTNESS and INTERFACE_ROBUSTNESS hold for every |S|<=k, then G-S is connected for every |S|<=k.
The explicit cut {z} union U for a minimum vertex cover U of X has size k+1 and disconnects c from f, hence disconnects G.
layer_2A_block_quotient_transfer_theorem.sharpness_note: This layer is sufficient, not necessary. It may fail when a block splits internally after k deletions even though the whole graph remains connected through external interfaces.

layer_2B_component_refined_transfer_theo.name: TWO_BLOCK_CHANNEL_LOCAL_TO_GLOBAL_TRANSFER_THEOREM__COMPONENT_REFINED
layer_2B_component_refined_transfer_theo.motivation: Remove unnecessary block-connectivity assumptions by quotienting actual surviving connected components.

definitions.deletion_budget: k=nu(X). Consider every S subseteq V(G) with |S|<=k.
surviving_modules: The singleton module {z} if z notin S.
refined_interface_graph_hat_BS: Create one quotient vertex for every surviving module.
Two quotient vertices are adjacent iff G-S contains at least one edge with endpoints in the two corresponding modules.

layer_2B_component_refined_transfer_theo.exact_quotient_lemma: For every S, without any block-robustness assumption, G-S is connected iff hat_B_S is connected.
theorem: If REFINED_INTERFACE_ROBUSTNESS holds for every |S|<=k, then G-S is connected for every |S|<=k.
The same explicit vertex-cover cut {z} union U gives kappa(G)<=k+1.
layer_2B_component_refined_transfer_theo.equivalence_form: Under the exact-channel interface, kappa(G)>=k+1 iff hat_B_S is connected for every S with |S|<=k.
layer_2B_component_refined_transfer_theo.role: This is the reusable sharp transfer layer for frames in which individual blocks may split under the deletion budget.

easy_sufficient_corollary.name: HIGH_BLOCK_CONNECTIVITY_PLUS_HUB_DEGREE_COROLLARY
assumptions: G[L] and G[R] remain connected after deletion of any at most k vertices from their own vertex sets (for example, each block has vertex connectivity at least k+1).
z has at least k+1 neighbors in L and at least k+1 neighbors in R.
E(L,R)=X and the exact-channel interface assumptions hold.
proof: If z notin S and |S|<=k, at least one z-neighbor survives in each block; block robustness then makes B_S connected through z.
If z in S, at most k-1 other vertices are deleted. Since tau(X)=nu(X)=k, those vertices cannot cover all X-edges; one cross-edge survives and joins the two connected blocks.
easy_sufficient_corollary.limitation: This easy corollary is intentionally stronger than the sharp component-refined theorem and need not cover deletion budgets at which a block itself can split.
